sentences.text:
This is the first application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) for grant of anticipatory bail apprehending his arrest in relation to Crime No.327/2025 registered at Police Station - Junnardeo, District Chhindwara (M.P.)
for the offence punishable under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B of IPC.
2.

As per the prosecution story, the complainants Manoj Yadav and Vinod Yadav, are the sons of Late Smt. Lalta Bai Yaduvanshi, who had purchased land bearing Survey No. 483/9, area 0.300 hectare, through a registered sale deed dated 06.01.2003.
After her death in 2014, the land remained recorded in her name, and mutation was not carried out in favour of her legal heirs.

During the year 2024, the accused persons Satpal Pal, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:56062 2 MCRC-47585-2025 Indra Singh Chauhan, Malti Jaiswal, Chandrapal Pawar, Obesh Khan, and Ajesh Suryavanshi allegedly entered into a criminal conspiracy to fraudulently obtain ownership of the said land.

In furtherance of the conspiracy, they are said to have prepared a forged Aadhaar card in the name of Lalita Bai, using the photograph of accused Malti Jaiswal and thereby impersonated the deceased woman to get the land re-registered in the name of co-accused Indra Singh Chauhan before the Sub- Registrar, Junardeo.

On verification, it was found that the forged Aadhaar card bare the same photograph as Malti Jaiswal's genuine card,
confirming impersonation and forgery.
Therefore, the offence has been registered against the applicant and co-accused persons under aforesaid offences.
3. Learned senior counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.

It is submitted that the applicant is the bonafide purchaser of the Indrasingh Chouhan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183129930/
1 land.

sentences.text: No forged document has been made by the applicant.
The name of owner of the land is recorded as Lalita Bai Yaduvanshi in the revenue records.
It is further submitted that the applicant has paid Rs. five lacs for consideration of the sale deed.

It is also submitted that when the applicant came to know that the forgery has been committed, then he filed complaint to the Police Station,
Collector and Superintendent of Police.
The complaint was made before lodging of F.I.R., which shows the bonafides of applicant.
No offence is made out against the applicant.
There is no need of custodial interrogation of the applicant.
There is no criminal antecedents of the applicant.
The conclusion of trial will take considerable time.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:56062 3 MCRC-47585-2025 granted benefit of anticipatory bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for State has opposed the grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant and has submitted that the Lalita Bai was the real owner of the land.

The complainants Manoj Yadav and Vinod Yadav have stated in their statements that the applicant knew the Lalita Bai very well because she used to live in a hut near the field of applicant, therefore the father of applicant had harassed her for purchasing the said land.
The complainant Vinod stated in this statement that said land has been mortgaged to the applicant two times for marriage of his sister.
The other witnesses have also deposed against the applicant.
The custodial interrogation of the applicant is also required in this case.
Therefore, the applicant does not deserve grant of anticipatory bail.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6.
Looking to aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, I am not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
7. Accordingly, present MCRC stands dismissed.

(PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL) JUDGE mohsin Indrasingh Chouhan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183129930/
